{"batch":"theme-briefs-drain1-001","generated_at":"2026-10-26T12:00:00Z","authored_by":"session-lane","entries":[{"theme_id":"7ae77ef8-211a-4f20-ad88-341c8dcdae65","member_hash":"6820f32cec7cf8fbe867801365f6d17f","title":"Shipping decarbonisation: a global rule not yet adopted, dated buyer commitments and a fuel price shock","sections":{"connection":"Ocean shipping decarbonisation is being set from three sides at once. The research side finds the policy path short of its own marks: CO₂ emissions from shipping are projected to land between 729–768 MtCO₂ in 2030, representing only a 1–6% decrease below the 2008 reference emissions level. The buyer side has dated commitments from the First Movers Coalition. Carriers: Power at least 5% of deep-sea shipping with zero-emission fuels by 2030. Cargo owners: Internationally ship at least 10% of goods, in terms of volume, on ships using zero-emission fuels by 2030. The regulatory side sets a strategy mark for the same year: The strategy includes a commitment to ensure uptake of zero or near-zero GHG emission technologies, fuels and/or energy sources to represent at least 5%, striving for 10%, of the energy used by international shipping by 2030.","meaning":"A forwarder reads the three sides together. The research rating shows the policy path falling short, and the buyer coalition and the strategy name the same year for their marks. It is unclear how the postponement will affect the agreed technical measures of the NZF.

*Analytical inference:* until the global rules are settled, carrier selection is likelier to be questioned by buyers who hold dated commitments than by a single binding global rule; none of the members states that this reaches carrier selection, and this reading draws on the members cited here.","ramifications":"### Regulations
The rules in force are efficiency rules, and the text encourages and does not compel: Administrations, port authorities and other stakeholders as appropriate, are encouraged to provide incentives to ships rated as A or B. The global fuel framework is recorded only at the stage of draft approval: 7–11 April 2025: MEPC 83: Draft amendments to MARPOL Annex VI (IMO Net-Zero Framework) approved.

*Operational implication:* an operator planning against the strategy mark treats the encouragement of incentives for well-rated ships as an option open to port administrations, not as a duty on the operator.

### Market Intel
Dated buyer commitments are the nearer pressure on carriers: Carriers: Power at least 5% of deep-sea shipping with zero-emission fuels by 2030. Cargo owners: Internationally ship at least 10% of goods, in terms of volume, on ships using zero-emission fuels by 2030. Fuel markets also move on supply shocks: QatarEnergy declared force majeure on March 4, which has forced Asian buyers who import over 80% of Qatari gas to compete for spot cargoes on global markets to replace lost contract volumes.

### Research
The mission side sets production and fleet goals against the same horizon: Fuels Goal: Enable the production of 16 Mt of heavy fuel oil equivalent (HFOe) well-to-wake zero-emission fuels by 2030. Ships Goal: 600 large ships in international shipping are running on well-to-wake zero-emission fuel by 2030. The headline rating of the policy path is: CO₂ emissions from shipping are projected to land between 729–768 MtCO₂ in 2030, representing only a 1–6% decrease below the 2008 reference emissions level.","watch":"Watch the carbon intensity mark and the technical measures already agreed: 40% reduction in CO2 per transport work vs 2008 baseline (2023 IMO GHG Strategy)… It is unclear how the postponement will affect the agreed technical measures of the NZF. the makers, and the same cost and charging barriers across markets","sections":{"connection":"Road freight electrification is being pushed by vehicle rules, by buyers and trial results, and held back by cost and charging barriers that are named in more than one market. In Europe the vehicle rule is set on the makers: The EU's revised CO2 standards for heavy-duty vehicles were ratified by the Council of the European Union on 13 May 2024 and set reduction targets of 45% by 2030, 65% by 2035, and 90% by 2040 relative to a 2019 reporting baseline. The barriers named by the market side are: Identified deployment barriers as of 2022 include charging infrastructure density, purchase cost premium, range limitations, and small-fleet access. An operations profile for India names the same pair: The high upfront cost of electric trucks, coupled with limited charging infrastructure, remains a significant roadblock.","meaning":"A forwarder with road legs reads the vehicle rules and the barriers together. The rules set the pace at which new trucks are meant to become low emission; the barriers decide whether fleets can take them up.

*Analytical inference:* the pressure on road hauliers reaches them through the truck makers and through fleet rules where those exist, and through cost and charging access; the members do not state how this reaches a forwarder's carrier panel or rate.","ramifications":"### Regulations
The member titled California Advanced Clean Fleets Rule (CARB) records: The ACF Regulation was adopted by CARB in the 2023 rulemaking. The regulator also describes how it will treat early compliance: CARB is providing guidance to inform State and local government agencies that during the first reporting cycles of the amended ACF regulations, CARB will focus on supporting compliance on a case-by-case basis as agencies are making good faith efforts to comply.

### Market Intel
The market side gives the target path and the cost of the inputs: The EU's revised CO2 standards for heavy-duty vehicles were ratified by the Council of the European Union on 13 May 2024 and set reduction targets of 45% by 2030, 65% by 2035, and 90% by 2040 relative to a 2019 reporting baseline. Battery materials are part of the cost picture: Projections suggest a fivefold increase in demand for cobalt, graphite and lithium by 2050 due to their intensive use in new energy technologies. Identified deployment barriers as of 2022 include charging infrastructure density, purchase cost premium, range limitations, and small-fleet access.

### Research
Trial evidence is early and thin: DP World has successfully trialled three electric vehicles under the Project Jolt initiative, which it joined three months ago. The trial programme states the emissions stake: HGVs also account for 20% of CO 2 emissions from domestic transport. The research record also states a limit: The scarcity of non-technical research outside the autonomous car's realm means the equivalent environmental analysis for heavy freight vehicles on long-haul or international road corridors is not established in the sourced material.

### Operations
The operations profiles show what fleets face on the ground. In India: The high upfront cost of electric trucks, coupled with limited charging infrastructure, remains a significant roadblock. In July 2025, the Ministry of Heavy Industries released guidelines for electric trucks under the PM e-DRIVE scheme For the United States, the profile reports: Cars and light-duty trucks (including pickups and SUVs) are responsible for 57.5 percent of transportation emissions; medium- and heavy-duty vehicles produce about 26 percent of transportation emissions, per C2ES.","watch":"Watch the vehicle targets as they step down over the years: Operational implication: The HDV CO2 targets (45% by 2030, 65% by 2035, 90% by 2040) apply to truck manufacturers' new-vehicle fleets. while delivered charging capacity remains small","sections":{"connection":"Public bodies are building the planning and funding frame for cleaner road freight, and the evidence of delivered capacity is still thin. In the United States the coordinating body is described this way: The Joint Office of Energy and Transportation (Joint Office) was created through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and facilitates collaboration between the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) and the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT). The funding programmes behind public charging are: The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), within DOT, administers two programs that support public electric vehicle charging infrastructure: the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Formula Program (NEVI) and the Charging and Fueling Infrastructure Discretionary Grant Program (CFI). What the record shows as delivered is small against that frame: As of April 2025, 384 NEVI- and CFI-funded chargers were open to the public.","meaning":"A forwarder with road or intermodal legs reads the funding frame and the delivered count together. The frame is in place and the delivered base is narrow.

*Analytical inference:* planning for zero-emission road legs on these lanes can rely on public programmes existing, and cannot yet rely on public charging being widely open; the members do not state a date by which that changes.","ramifications":"### Regulations
State freight planning is tied to federal funding: In order to receive funding under the National Highway Freight Program (23 U.S.C. 167), the FAST Act requires each State to develop a State freight plan. The federal check is stated for updates: The FHWA monitors and approves all State Freight Plan updates to ensure compliance with current federal surface transportation laws. A court ruling is also recorded: In January 2026, District Judge Tana Lin issued a final judgment on January 30, 2026 in Washington v. U.S. Department of Transportation, determining USDOT's February-to-August pause of the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program to be a violation of the Administrative Procedure Act.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* what the judgment means for any state charging award or for a private bidder is for counsel.

### Market Intel
Private companies are invited into the programmes: Private sector companies are invited to bid into the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) Formula Program and Charging and Fueling Infrastructure Program opportunities released by states and communities. The delivered base as recorded is: As of April 2025, 384 NEVI- and CFI-funded chargers were open to the public.

### Research
Research members put numbers on efficiency from different angles: Moving freight on battery-electric rail vehicles can use 75% less energy per mile than moving it on a semitruck. MIT CTL research published across 25 cities on 6 continents finds that elevation-aware routing can significantly reduce CO₂ on urban truck legs.

### Operations
The operations members show planning in practice. In Abu Dhabi: ADNOC Distribution has committed through its mobility arm E2GO to building 70,000 charging points by 2030. For a United States state plan, the Louisiana profile states: The Louisiana State Freight Plan is intended to: meet federal guidelines and support future planning, policies, and investment in Louisiana; support the business case for freight system investments; promote safe, efficient, and resilient goods mobility and supply chain support in Louisiana; develop data to support local and regional mobility planning; and reflect input from private sector freight stakeholders.","watch":"Watch the charging build-out against its dated commitment: In Abu Dhabi, ADNOC Distribution has committed through its mobility arm E2GO to building 70,000 charging points by 2030.
